items.body:
## Define the guest and the occasion

A hotel serving business travel, a leisure resort and a banquet-led property have different operating requirements. Set out the intended guest, stay pattern and role of rooms, food and beverage, events and other facilities.

## Bring operations into design

The design brief should address guest movement, service circulation, storage, kitchens, housekeeping and maintenance alongside the visible experience. Review these interfaces with the relevant design and operating professionals.

## Connect the budget to the programme

Separate building works, interiors, equipment, operating supplies and pre-opening requirements. Track responsibilities, dependencies and decision dates so that a late specification or approval does not become a surprise at handover.

## Treat opening as a workstream

Opening readiness includes staffing, training, operating procedures, supplies, systems and testing. Define acceptance criteria and the handover evidence required from each appointed party.

items.body:
## Keep the requirement identifiable

Assign each requirement a stable line reference. Record the intended use, specification, unit of measure and quantity. Preserve that reference through vendor responses, substitutions, approvals and orders.

## Distinguish a match from a substitution

A similar description does not necessarily represent the same product. Compare material, dimensions, capacity, finish, accessories, warranty and service scope. Identify deviations explicitly and obtain approval before treating alternatives as equivalent.

## Compare the complete commercial basis

Keep base price, taxes, freight, installation and other charges separately visible. Compare minimum quantities, lead times, payment terms and delivery locations alongside price. Mark unquoted lines rather than assigning assumed rates.

## Close the loop with an approval record

Record the selected specification, sample approval, commercial terms and delivery requirement. A change after selection should create a new version so the project team can identify what was ordered and why.

items.body:
## Start with the decision

An owner considering a sale, a development partnership or refinancing is asking three different questions. Define the intended outcome, the time available and the constraints before preparing a presentation or beginning counterparty outreach.

## Build one consistent fact base

Bring the asset description, area measurements, ownership information, approvals, leases and financial records into a controlled information set. Separate a documented fact from a management estimate and an adviser’s assumption. Record the date and source of each important figure.

## Make the commercial case inspectable

Show how revenue, costs, capital expenditure and timing support the proposed transaction. Explain sensitivities and information gaps. A polished memorandum is most useful when the underlying assumptions can be followed.

## Sequence disclosure

An introductory teaser and a detailed diligence room serve different purposes. Agree what can be disclosed at each stage, who can receive it and how questions will be tracked. Specialist advisers should review matters within their respective scopes.

items.body:
India Gully is a brand of Vivacious Entertainment and Hospitality Private Limited, incorporated in 2017. We work with owners, promoters, investors and operators at the intersection of real estate, hospitality and business.

Our work begins with the commercial question: what should an asset become, who is the right partner, how should a transaction be prepared, and what will it take to deliver? We bring together advisory, market engagement and execution support to answer those questions in context.

“Celebrating Desiness” reflects our Indian roots and the entrepreneurial spirit of the businesses we serve. It sits alongside a disciplined approach to information, accountability and delivery.

Amit leads India Gully’s real estate practice, combining transaction experience with a detailed understanding of retail destinations, leasing economics and asset positioning.

## Market experience

With more than 15 years of experience, his work spans acquisitions, investments, leasing and asset management. His professional experience includes engagements associated with Gardens Galleria, Hyatt Andaz, AIPL Joy Street and Entertainment City Limited.

## At India Gully

Amit works with property owners, developers, investors and occupiers to define the commercial brief, identify suitable counterparties and coordinate negotiations. He brings particular focus to retail and commercial assets, tenant mix, income potential and the practical requirements of execution.

His role connects market intelligence with active mandate delivery, from initial opportunity assessment through commercial discussions and transaction coordination.

Arun founded India Gully to bring commercial advisory and hands-on execution into one practice. His work spans asset strategy, transactions, hospitality development and the operating decisions that determine long-term value.

## Experience and perspective

With more than 20 years of experience across real estate, hospitality and entertainment, Arun brings a promoter’s understanding of business priorities alongside an adviser’s discipline in preparing and executing transactions. His leadership experience includes Entertainment City Limited, Noida, home to The Great India Place, Gardens Galleria and Worlds of Wonder.

## At India Gully

Arun leads the firm’s strategy, senior client relationships and complex mandates. He works with promoters, asset owners, investors and operating partners to assess opportunities, structure the commercial approach and coordinate the work required to move from an initial brief to a considered decision.

His focus includes real estate transactions, hospitality feasibility and operator strategy, development partnerships, debt advisory and special situations.

Pavan connects hospitality operations with project delivery and procurement. He brings more than 18 years of sector experience to the practical questions of operating standards, brand requirements, equipment selection and opening readiness.

## Hospitality experience

His experience includes work across hospitality environments associated with Mahindra Holidays, Accor, CGH Earth and WelcomHeritage. This operating perspective informs the way India Gully approaches hotel briefs, vendor coordination and the detail of guest-facing delivery.

## At India Gully

Pavan leads hospitality operations and HORECA engagement, working with owners, operators and suppliers to align specifications, budgets and delivery requirements. His remit includes brand onboarding support, furniture, fixtures and equipment, operating supplies and project procurement.

He helps clients translate a hospitality concept into an actionable sourcing and delivery programme, with attention to quality, suitability and coordination.
